original_question: Determine conditions on a germ f in End(C^3,O) guaranteeing existence of a modification pi: M~ -> C^3 based at O, a point p in E=pi^{-1}(O), and a (possibly weakly) rigid germ f~ in End(M,p) such that pi o f~ = f o pi.
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Open Problem (OP12): the 3-dimensional rigidification problem for non-invertible germs.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact open problem. It correctly identifies the ambient space C^3, the existence of a modification pi based at O, a point p over O, a lifted germ f~, the possibility of asking only for weak rigidity, and the semiconjugacy relation pi o f~ = f o pi. It also correctly aims at existence of a birational/modified rigidification, not at classification of rigid germs themselves.
missing_details: The official target in the paper is not a theorem or conjecture but Open Problem (OP12) in Section 3.3.
End(C^3, O) should be spelled out as the set of germs of holomorphic self-maps of C^3 fixing O.

The nearby context makes clear that this question is really meaningful for non-invertible dominant germs; dominant means det Jac(f) is not identically zero, while invertible and non-dominant germs are trivially rigid.
The paper defines Crit^infty(f) explicitly as union_{k>=0} f^{-k}(Crit(f)) = union_{k>=0} Crit(f^k); this should be included if the question is to be stand-alone.
The meaning of weakly rigid is missing: Crit^infty(f), as a germ at the origin, must be a union of 0 <= q <= dim M smooth irreducible components having simple normal crossings.

The stronger meaning of rigid is missing: if W_1, ..., W_q are the irreducible components of Crit^infty(f), then for each j there must exist I_j subset of {1, ..., q} such that f(W_j) = intersection_{i in I_j} W_i.
The meaning of modification is missing: pi: M~ -> M is a surjective holomorphic map obtained as a finite composition of blow-ups of submanifolds or points.
The meaning of 'based at O' is missing: the first blow-up center contains O, and each later blow-up center meets the inverse image of O.
It should be explicit that M~ is a complex 3-dimensional manifold and p lies in the exceptional fibre E = pi^{-1}(O).
It should be explicit that f~ is a holomorphic germ in End(M~, p) and the identity pi o f~ = f o pi is an equality of germs near p and O.
refined_question: For which non-invertible dominant holomorphic germs f in End(C^3, O) — where End(C^3, O) denotes germs of holomorphic self-maps of C^3 fixing O, and dominant means det Jac(f) is not identically zero — does there exist a modification pi: M~ -> C^3 based at O (i.e. a finite composition of blow-ups of submanifolds or points whose first center contains O and whose later centers meet the inverse image of O), a point p in E := pi^{-1}(O), and a holomorphic germ f~ in End(M~, p) such that pi o f~ = f o pi and f~ is rigid, or at least weakly rigid, in the sense that Crit^infty(f~) = union_{k>=0} Crit(f~^k) = union_{k>=0} f~^{-k}(Crit(f~)) is, as a germ at p, a union of smooth irreducible components with simple normal crossings, and in the rigid case each irreducible component W_j of Crit^infty(f~) satisfies f~(W_j) = intersection_{i in I_j} W_i for some I_j subset of {1, ..., q}?
justification: arXiv:1107.4876 is Abate's survey 'Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics', and your draft matches almost verbatim the official Open Problem OP12 in Section 3.3. The precise nearby context needed to make the question stand-alone is supplied by Definition 13 (Crit^infty, weakly rigid, rigid), Definition 14 (modification; based at a point), the sentence noting that the notion is interesting only for non-invertible dominant germs, and Theorem 12 giving the exact 2-dimensional precedent that motivates OP12. Definition 11 provides the paper's meaning of 'dominant', and Definition 1 fixes the meaning of End(M, p) as germs of holomorphic self-maps fixing the base point.
